links.comparator_used: Phase I physician directives made without AI assistance (pre-AI, 60 retrospective cases), compared with Phase II AI-guided directives (60 prospective cases)
links.outcome: Plan achievability (achieved plan within ±3 Gy of physician directive), first-plan acceptance, plan iterations, and OAR dose
links.effect: Plan achievability rose from 52.9% to 80.4%. Physician acceptance of the first plan rose from 63.3% to 90%. Maximum plan iterations fell from 4 to 2. Spinal cord, inferior constrictor, larynx and oral cavity doses fell significantly (range 4.3 to 15.2 Gy).
links.tradeoff: Esophagus and contralateral parotid doses rose by 2.3 to 3.1 Gy, not statistically significant. Planning time data were not sufficient to measure efficiency. Phase I and Phase II used different cases, with systematic dose differences in some OARs. Oral cavity dose was slightly higher than the AI-guided directive.
links.quote: Overall, implementation of the AI assistant improved achieved increased plan uniformity and quality comparing to planning without AI guidance.

design_hint: AI dose predictor as physician decision support tool to guide treatment directives
